definitions.gloss: pounded burdock root dressed with sesame
definitions.explanation: A New Year dish of burdock root that is boiled, lightly pounded to split it, cut into short lengths, and dressed with ground sesame and vinegar. One of the three celebratory dishes of {関西|かんさい}-style おせち{料理|りょうり}.

examples.japanese: たたきごぼうを{作|つく}った。
おせちにはたたきごぼうが{欠|か}かせない。
examples.english: Tataki-gobo is indispensable in our New Year food.

examples.japanese: {関西|かんさい}では、{黒豆|くろまめ}、{数|かず}の{子|こ}、たたきごぼうの{三品|さんぴん}をそろえる{家庭|かてい}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: In the Kansai region, many households prepare the three dishes of black beans, herring roe, and tataki-gobo.

notes:
Written たたきごぼう or {叩|たた}きごぼう. From {叩|たた}く (to strike) plus ごぼう (burdock root): the boiled root is tapped with a pestle so that it splits and takes up the dressing.

CULTURAL CONTEXT:
Burdock grows straight and deep, so the dish stands for a family taking firm root and prospering. In {関西|かんさい} it is one of the three celebratory dishes ({三|み}つ{肴|ざかな}) served at New Year, alongside {黒豆|くろまめ} and {数|かず}の{子|こ}; in {関東|かんとう} its place is taken by {田作|たづく}り.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- たたきごぼうを{作|つく}る: to make tataki-gobo
- ごま{和|あ}えのたたきごぼう: tataki-gobo dressed with sesame
- おせちのたたきごぼう: the tataki-gobo in the New Year food
